chapters.summary: Jesus warns His disciples against the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy, and teaches them not to fear those who can kill the body. He tells the parable of the rich fool who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God, and urges His followers to be watchful and ready for the Son of man's coming.

verses.kjv: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
verses.modern: At that time, some people told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

verses.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?
verses.modern: Jesus answered them, "Do You think those Galileans were worse sinners than all other Galileans, because they suffered this way?

verses.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
verses.modern: No, I tell You. But unless You repent, You will all likewise perish.

verses.kjv: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
verses.modern: Or those eighteen on whom the tower of Siloam fell and killed them — do You think they were worse sinners than all others who lived in Jerusalem?

verses.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
verses.modern: No, I tell You. But unless You repent, You will all likewise perish."

verses.kjv: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.
verses.modern: He also told this parable: "A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.

verses.kjv: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?
verses.modern: He said to the keeper of his vineyard, 'Three years now I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and found none. Cut it down. Why should it use up the ground?'

verses.kjv: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:
verses.modern: The keeper answered Him, 'Sir, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.

verses.kjv: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.
verses.modern: If it bears fruit next year, good. If not, then cut it down.' "

verses.kjv: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
verses.modern: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

verses.kjv: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.
verses.modern: There was a woman who had a spirit of illness for eighteen years. She was bent double and could not straighten up at all.

verses.kjv: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.
verses.modern: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said to her, "Woman, You are set free from Your illness."

verses.kjv: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
verses.modern: He laid His hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and praised God.

verses.kjv: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.
verses.modern: The ruler of the synagogue was angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. He said to the people, "There are six days in which people ought to work. Come on those days and be healed — not on the Sabbath day."

verses.kjv: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
verses.modern: The Lord answered Him, "You hypocrite! Does not each of You on the Sabbath untie His ox or his donkey from the stall and lead it away to water?

verses.kjv: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
verses.modern: Should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound for eighteen years, be set free from this bond on the Sabbath day?"

verses.kjv: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
verses.modern: When He said this, all His opponents were put to shame. All the people rejoiced at the wonderful things he was doing.

verses.kjv: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?
verses.modern: Then He said, "What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?

verses.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.
verses.modern: It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air made nests in its branches."

verses.kjv: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?
verses.modern: Again He said, "What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?

verses.kjv: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
verses.modern: It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour until the whole batch was leavened."

verses.kjv: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
verses.modern: He traveled through towns and villages, teaching as He made His way to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,
verses.modern: Someone asked him, "Lord, will only a few be saved?" He said to them,

verses.kjv: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
verses.modern: "Strive to enter through the narrow gate. Many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.

verses.kjv: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:
verses.modern: Once the master of the house rises and shuts the door, you will stand outside and knock, saying, 'Lord, Lord, open to us.' He will answer, 'I do not know where you are from.'

verses.kjv: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
verses.modern: Then you will say, 'We ate and drank in Your presence. You taught in our streets.'

verses.kjv: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
verses.modern: He will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from Me, all you workers of iniquity.'

verses.kjv: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
verses.modern: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God — but you yourselves cast out.

verses.kjv: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.
verses.modern: People will come from east and west, from north and south, and will take their places at the feast in the kingdom of God.

verses.kjv: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.
verses.modern: Indeed, there are those who are last who will be first, and those who are first who will be last."

verses.kjv: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
verses.modern: At that very hour some Pharisees came and said to Him, "Leave this place and go away, for Herod wants to kill you."

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
verses.modern: He said to them, "Go tell that fox, 'I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.'

verses.kjv: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Still, I must go on today and tomorrow and the next day — for it cannot be that a prophet should perish away from Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
verses.modern: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings — but you would not!

verses.kjv: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
verses.modern: Your house is left to you desolate. Truly I say to you, you will not see Me until you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.' "

chapters.summary: Jesus warns that unless the people repent, they will likewise perish, and He tells the parable of the barren fig tree. He heals a woman bent over for eighteen years on the Sabbath, teaches about the narrow gate, and laments over Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.
verses.modern: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the house of a prominent Pharisee, and they were watching Him closely.

verses.kjv: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.
verses.modern: There in front of Him was a man who had dropsy.

verses.kjv: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
verses.modern: Jesus asked the lawyers and Pharisees, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day, or not?"

verses.kjv: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;
verses.modern: They were silent. So He took the man, healed him, and sent him away.

verses.kjv: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
verses.modern: Then He said to them, "Which of you, if your ass or your ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him out?"

verses.kjv: And they could not answer him again to these things.
verses.modern: They could not reply to this.

verses.kjv: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,
verses.modern: When He noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable.

verses.kjv: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;
verses.modern: "When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit down in the place of honor. A more distinguished man than you may have been invited.

verses.kjv: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.
verses.modern: The host who invited both of you will come and say, 'Give this man your seat.' Then you will have to take the lowest seat in shame.

verses.kjv: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.
verses.modern: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place. Then your host will come and say, 'Friend, move up to a better place.' That will bring you honor in front of everyone at the table.

verses.kjv: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
verses.modern: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted."

verses.kjv: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.
verses.modern: He also said to the man who had invited him, "When you give a dinner or a supper, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbors. They may invite you back and repay you.

verses.kjv: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:
verses.modern: But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
verses.modern: You will be blessed, because they cannot repay you. You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."

verses.kjv: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
verses.modern: When one of those at the table heard this, He said to Jesus, "Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!"

verses.kjv: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:
verses.modern: Jesus replied, "A man gave a great banquet and invited many people.

verses.kjv: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.
verses.modern: At the time of the banquet, He sent His servant to tell those invited, 'Come, for everything is now ready.'

verses.kjv: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.
verses.modern: But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said, 'I have bought a field, and I must go see it. Please excuse me.'

verses.kjv: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.
verses.modern: Another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.'

verses.kjv: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.
verses.modern: Another said, 'I have just married a wife, and so I cannot come.'

verses.kjv: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
verses.modern: The servant came and reported this to his master. The master of the house became angry and said to His servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city and bring in the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.'

verses.kjv: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
verses.modern: The servant said, 'Sir, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.'

verses.kjv: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
verses.modern: The master said to the servant, 'Go out to the roads and country lanes and make them come in, so that my house will be full.

verses.kjv: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.
verses.modern: I tell You, not one of those who were invited will taste my banquet.' "

verses.kjv: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,
verses.modern: Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. He turned and said to them,

verses.kjv: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
verses.modern: "If anyone comes to Me and does not love Me more than his father and mother, his wife and children, His brothers and sisters — yes, even His own life — he cannot be My disciple.

verses.kjv: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
verses.modern: Whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.

verses.kjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
verses.modern: Which of You, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost — whether He has enough to complete it?

verses.kjv: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
verses.modern: Otherwise, if He lays the foundation and cannot finish, everyone who sees it will mock Him,

verses.kjv: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
verses.modern: saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to finish.'

verses.kjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
verses.modern: Or what king, going to war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he can meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand — when he himself has only ten thousand?

verses.kjv: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.
verses.modern: If he cannot, he sends a delegation while the other king is still far away and asks for terms of peace.

verses.kjv: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
verses.modern: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.

verses.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?
verses.modern: Salt is good. But if salt loses its flavor, how can it be made salty again?

verses.kjv: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.modern: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile — it is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."

chapters.summary: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath in the house of a Pharisee and teaches about humility at feasts. He tells the parable of the great supper, where those first invited refuse and the poor and outcast are brought in, and warns that those who follow Him must count the cost.

verses.kjv: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.
verses.modern: All the tax collectors and sinners were coming near to hear Him.

verses.kjv: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
verses.modern: The Pharisees and scribes grumbled, saying, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."

verses.kjv: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,
verses.modern: So He told them this parable:

verses.kjv: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
verses.modern: "Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost one until he finds it?

verses.kjv: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.modern: When he finds it, he joyfully lifts it onto his shoulders.

verses.kjv: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
verses.modern: When he arrives home, he calls his friends and neighbors together and says, 'Rejoice with me! I have found my lost sheep.'

verses.kjv: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
verses.modern: I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

verses.kjv: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?
verses.modern: Or what woman, having ten silver coins and losing one, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?

verses.kjv: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
verses.modern: When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, 'Rejoice with me! I have found the coin I had lost.'

verses.kjv: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
verses.modern: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."

verses.kjv: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
verses.modern: He also said, "A man had two sons.

verses.kjv: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
verses.modern: The younger one said to his father, 'Father, give me my share of the estate.' So the father divided his property between them.

verses.kjv: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
verses.modern: Not long after, the younger son gathered everything together and traveled to a distant country. There he squandered his wealth with wild living.

verses.kjv: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
verses.modern: When he had spent everything, a severe famine struck that whole country, and he began to be in need.

verses.kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
verses.modern: He went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

verses.kjv: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
verses.modern: He longed to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.

verses.kjv: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
verses.modern: When he came to his senses, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have more than enough food, and here I am starving to death!

verses.kjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
verses.modern: I will get up and go to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

verses.kjv: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
verses.modern: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants." '

verses.kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.modern: So he got up and went to his father. While he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, threw his arms around him, and kissed him.

verses.kjv: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
verses.modern: The son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'

verses.kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
verses.modern: But the father said to his servants, 'Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

verses.kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
verses.modern: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us eat and celebrate!

verses.kjv: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
verses.modern: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.' And they began to celebrate.

verses.kjv: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.
verses.modern: Now the older son was in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.

verses.kjv: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
verses.modern: He called one of the servants and asked what was happening.

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.
verses.modern: The servant told him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he received him back safe and well.'

verses.kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
verses.modern: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

verses.kjv: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
verses.modern: The son answered his father, 'Look, all these years I have worked for you and never disobeyed your commands. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

verses.kjv: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
verses.modern: But when this son of yours, who has wasted your property with prostitutes, came back — you killed the fattened calf for him!'

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.
verses.modern: The father said to him, 'Son, you have always been with me, and everything I have is yours.

verses.kjv: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
verses.modern: But it was right that we should celebrate and be glad. For this brother of yours was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.' "

chapters.summary: Jesus tells three parables about what was lost and found: the parable of the lost sheep, the parable of the lost coin, and the parable of the prodigal son. In each parable there is great joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.

verses.kjv: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.
verses.modern: Jesus also said to His disciples: "There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting His possessions.

verses.kjv: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.
verses.modern: He called the manager in and said, 'What is this I hear about You? Give an account of Your management, because You can no longer be manager.'

verses.kjv: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.
verses.modern: The manager said to himself, 'What will I do? My master is taking away my job. I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.

verses.kjv: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
verses.modern: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from this position, people will welcome me into their homes.'

verses.kjv: So he called every one of his lord's debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?
verses.modern: He called in each of his master's debtors. He asked the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'

verses.kjv: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
verses.modern: 'Eight hundred gallons of olive oil,' he replied. The manager said, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write four hundred.'

verses.kjv: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.
verses.modern: Then he asked another, 'And how much do you owe?' 'A thousand bushels of wheat,' he replied. He said, 'Take your bill and write eight hundred.'

verses.kjv: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
verses.modern: The master commended the dishonest manager for acting shrewdly. For the people of this world are shrewder in dealing with their own kind than the people of the light.

verses.kjv: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
verses.modern: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it fails, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

verses.kjv: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
verses.modern: Whoever is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much. Whoever is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.

verses.kjv: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
verses.modern: If then you have not been faithful in the use of worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?

verses.kjv: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man's, who shall give you that which is your own?
verses.modern: And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?

verses.kjv: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
verses.modern: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money."

verses.kjv: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
verses.modern: The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and were sneering at Jesus.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
verses.modern: He said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves in the sight of men. But God knows Your hearts. What is highly valued among men is an abomination in God's sight.

verses.kjv: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
verses.modern: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the good news of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is pressing into it.

verses.kjv: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
verses.modern: It is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for the smallest part of the Law to fall away.

verses.kjv: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.
verses.modern: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. And everyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.

verses.kjv: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
verses.modern: There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.

verses.kjv: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
verses.modern: At his gate lay a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores.

verses.kjv: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.modern: He longed to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
verses.modern: The beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's side. The rich man also died and was buried.

verses.kjv: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
verses.modern: In hell, the rich man was in torment. He looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus at his side.

verses.kjv: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
verses.modern: He called out, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in agony in this fire.'

verses.kjv: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
verses.modern: But Abraham replied, 'Son, remember that in your lifetime you received good things, while Lazarus received evil things. But now he is comforted here, and you are in agony.

verses.kjv: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
verses.modern: Besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you. Those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross over from there to us.'

verses.kjv: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house:
verses.modern: Then he said, 'Then I beg you, father, send Lazarus to my father's house,

verses.kjv: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
verses.modern: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.'

verses.kjv: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
verses.modern: Abraham replied, 'They have Moses and the Prophets. Let them listen to them.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.
verses.modern: 'No, father Abraham,' he said, 'but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
verses.modern: Abraham said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.' "

chapters.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the unjust steward and teaches about faithfulness in that which is least and the impossibility of serving both God and mammon. He tells of the rich man and Lazarus, where the rich man dies and is tormented in hell while Lazarus rests in Abraham's bosom.

verses.kjv: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!
verses.modern: Jesus said to His disciples, "It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come — but woe to the one through whom they come!

verses.kjv: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.
verses.modern: It would be better for Him to have a millstone hung around His neck and be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

verses.kjv: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
verses.modern: Watch yourselves. If Your brother sins against You, rebuke Him. If He repents, forgive Him.

verses.kjv: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
verses.modern: Even if He sins against You seven times in a day and seven times comes back to You saying, 'I repent,' you must forgive Him."

verses.kjv: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
verses.modern: The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith!"

verses.kjv: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.
verses.modern: The Lord replied, "If You had faith as small as a grain of mustard seed, You could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey You.

verses.kjv: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?
verses.modern: Which of You, having a servant who is plowing or tending sheep, will say to Him when He comes in from the field, 'Come right in and sit down to eat'?

verses.kjv: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
verses.modern: Will He not say instead, 'Prepare my supper, get dressed and serve me while I eat and drink — and after that You may eat and drink'?

verses.kjv: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.
verses.modern: Does He thank the servant because he did what was commanded? I think not.

verses.kjv: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
verses.modern: So You also, when You have done everything commanded of You, say, 'We are unworthy servants. We have only done our duty.' "

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
verses.modern: As Jesus made His way to Jerusalem, He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.

verses.kjv: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
verses.modern: As He entered a village, ten men who had leprosy met Him. They stood at a distance

verses.kjv: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
verses.modern: and cried out in a loud voice, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"

verses.kjv: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
verses.modern: When He saw them, He said, "Go, show yourselves to the priests." And as they went, they were cleansed.

verses.kjv: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
verses.modern: One of them, when He saw that He was healed, came back, praising God in a loud voice.

verses.kjv: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
verses.modern: He fell on His face at Jesus' feet and thanked Him. And He was a Samaritan.

verses.kjv: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
verses.modern: Jesus asked, "Were not ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?

verses.kjv: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
verses.modern: Has no one returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?"

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
verses.modern: Then He said to Him, "Rise and go. Your faith has made You well."

verses.kjv: And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:
verses.modern: When the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come, He answered, "The kingdom of God does not come with signs to be observed.

verses.kjv: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
verses.modern: People will not say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'There it is!' For the kingdom of God is within You."

verses.kjv: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.
verses.modern: Then He said to the disciples, "The time will come when You will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but You will not see it.

verses.kjv: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
verses.modern: People will say, 'Look there!' or 'Look here!' Do not go after them or follow them.

verses.kjv: For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.
verses.modern: For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will the Son of Man be in His day.

verses.kjv: But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation.
verses.modern: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

verses.kjv: And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
verses.modern: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be in the days of the Son of Man.

verses.kjv: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
verses.modern: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, right up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.

verses.kjv: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
verses.modern: It was the same in the days of Lot. People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.

verses.kjv: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
verses.modern: But the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.

verses.kjv: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
verses.modern: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

verses.kjv: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
verses.modern: On that day, no one on the housetop, with belongings in the house, should come down to take them. Likewise, no one in the field should turn back.

verses.kjv: Remember Lot's wife.
verses.modern: Remember Lot's wife!

verses.kjv: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.
verses.modern: Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will preserve it.

verses.kjv: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
verses.modern: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed. One will be taken and the other left.

verses.kjv: Two women shall be grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
verses.modern: Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other left.

verses.kjv: Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
verses.modern: Two men will be in the field. One will be taken and the other left.

verses.kjv: And they answered and said unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.
verses.modern: They asked Him, "Where, Lord?" He said to them, "Where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together."

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches His disciples about offenses, forgiveness, and faith, telling them that faith the size of a mustard seed can uproot a tree. He cleanses ten lepers, and only one — a Samaritan — returns to give thanks. He teaches about the coming of the kingdom of God and the day of the Son of man.

verses.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
verses.modern: Jesus told them a parable to show that they should always pray and not give up.

verses.kjv: Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man:
verses.modern: He said, "In a certain city there was a judge who neither feared God nor cared about people.

verses.kjv: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.
verses.modern: In that city there was a widow who kept coming to Him, saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'

verses.kjv: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;
verses.modern: For a while He refused. But finally He said to Himself, 'Though I neither fear God nor care about people,

verses.kjv: Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.
verses.modern: yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice — so that she will not wear me out by her constant coming.' "

verses.kjv: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.
verses.modern: The Lord said, "Hear what the unrighteous judge says.

verses.kjv: And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?
verses.modern: Will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones, who cry out to Him day and night? Will He keep putting them off?

verses.kjv: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
verses.modern: I tell You, He will see that they get justice quickly. Yet when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?"

verses.kjv: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:
verses.modern: He also told this parable to some who were confident in their own righteousness and looked down on everyone else:

verses.kjv: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
verses.modern: "Two men went up to the temple to pray — one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

verses.kjv: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
verses.modern: The Pharisee stood and prayed about himself: 'God, I thank You that I am not like other men — robbers, evildoers, adulterers — or even like this tax collector.

verses.kjv: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
verses.modern: I fast twice a week and give a tenth of all I get.'

verses.kjv: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
verses.modern: But the tax collector stood far away. He would not even lift His eyes toward heaven, but beat His chest and said, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'

verses.kjv: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
verses.modern: I tell you, this man went home justified before God — not the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted."

verses.kjv: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
verses.modern: People were bringing babies to Jesus for Him to touch. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.

verses.kjv: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
verses.modern: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, "Let the little children come to Me and do not stop them. For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

verses.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.
verses.modern: Truly I say to You, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it."

verses.kjv: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
verses.modern: A certain ruler asked Him, "Good Master, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"

verses.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God.
verses.modern: Jesus replied, "Why do You call Me good? No one is good except God alone.

verses.kjv: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.
verses.modern: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor Your father and mother.' "

verses.kjv: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up.
verses.modern: The ruler said, "All these I have kept since I was a boy."

verses.kjv: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
verses.modern: When Jesus heard this, He said to Him, "You still lack one thing. Sell everything You have and give to the poor, and You will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me."

verses.kjv: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.
verses.modern: When the ruler heard this, He became very sorrowful, for He was very wealthy.

verses.kjv: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.modern: Jesus looked at Him and said, "How hard it is for the wealthy to enter the kingdom of God!

verses.kjv: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.modern: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."

verses.kjv: And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved?
verses.modern: Those who heard this asked, "Who then can be saved?"

verses.kjv: And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.
verses.modern: Jesus replied, "What is impossible with men is possible with God."

verses.kjv: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.
verses.modern: Peter said, "We have left everything we had to follow You!"

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God's sake,
verses.modern: Jesus said to them, "Truly I say to You, there is no one who has left house or parents or brothers or wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God

verses.kjv: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.
verses.modern: who will not receive many times as much in this age — and in the age to come, eternal life."

verses.kjv: Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.
verses.modern: Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, "We are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.

verses.kjv: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on:
verses.modern: He will be handed over to the Gentiles. They will mock Him, insult Him, and spit on Him.

verses.kjv: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
verses.modern: They will flog Him and kill Him. On the third day He will rise again."

verses.kjv: And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.
verses.modern: The disciples understood none of this. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not know what He was talking about.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:
verses.modern: As Jesus approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.

verses.kjv: And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant.
verses.modern: When He heard the crowd going by, He asked what was happening.

verses.kjv: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.
verses.modern: They told Him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."

verses.kjv: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
verses.modern: He called out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

verses.kjv: And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
verses.modern: Those who led the way rebuked him and told him to be quiet. But he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

verses.kjv: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,
verses.modern: Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked Him,

verses.kjv: Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
verses.modern: "What do You want Me to do for You?" He said, "Lord, I want to see."

verses.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee.
verses.modern: Jesus said to Him, "Receive Your sight. Your faith has saved You."

verses.kjv: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.
verses.modern: Immediately He received His sight and followed Jesus, praising God. When all the people saw it, they also praised God.

chapters.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the persistent widow and the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector who went up to the temple to pray. He blesses little children, tells a rich ruler to sell all he has, foretells His death and resurrection, and heals a blind man near Jericho.

verses.kjv: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
verses.modern: Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.

verses.kjv: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
verses.modern: There was a man there named Zacchaeus. He was the chief tax collector, and He was wealthy.

verses.kjv: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
verses.modern: He wanted to see who Jesus was, but He could not, because the crowd was too large. He was short in stature.

verses.kjv: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
verses.modern: So He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, because He was about to pass that way.

verses.kjv: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
verses.modern: When Jesus came to the place, He looked up and said to Him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at Your house today."

verses.kjv: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
verses.modern: He hurried and came down, and received Him joyfully.

verses.kjv: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
verses.modern: All the people saw this and began to grumble, saying, "He has gone to be a guest with a man who is a sinner."

verses.kjv: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
verses.modern: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor. And if I have taken anything from anyone by false accusation, I will restore it fourfold."

verses.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
verses.modern: Jesus said to Him, "Today salvation has come to this house, since He also is a son of Abraham."

verses.kjv: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
verses.modern: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.

verses.kjv: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.
verses.modern: As they were listening to these things, He went on to tell a parable. He was near Jerusalem, and they thought the kingdom of God was going to appear at any moment.

verses.kjv: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
verses.modern: He said, "A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for Himself and then return."

verses.kjv: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.
verses.modern: He called His ten servants and gave them ten pounds, saying to them, 'Do business with this until I come back.'

verses.kjv: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.
verses.modern: But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
verses.modern: When he returned, having received the kingdom, he commanded the servants to whom he had given the money to be called before him. He wanted to know how much each one had gained by trading.

verses.kjv: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.
verses.modern: The first came and said, 'Lord, your pound has made ten more pounds.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
verses.modern: He said to him, 'Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you will have authority over ten cities.'

verses.kjv: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.
verses.modern: The second came and said, 'Lord, your pound has made five more pounds.'

verses.kjv: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.
verses.modern: He said to him as well, 'You will be over five cities.'

verses.kjv: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:
verses.modern: Another came and said, 'Lord, here is your pound. I kept it stored away in a cloth.'

verses.kjv: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.
verses.modern: 'I was afraid of you, because you are a strict man. You take up what you did not put down, and you reap what you did not sow.'

verses.kjv: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:
verses.modern: He said to him, 'I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant. You knew that I was a strict man, taking up what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow.'

verses.kjv: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?
verses.modern: 'Therefore, why did you not put my money in the bank? Then at my coming I could have collected it with interest.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.
verses.modern: He said to those standing nearby, 'Take the pound from him and give it to the one who has ten pounds.'

verses.kjv: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)
verses.modern: They said to him, 'Lord, he already has ten pounds.'

verses.kjv: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.
verses.modern: 'I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given. But from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away.'

verses.kjv: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.
verses.modern: 'But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them — bring them here and kill them in my presence.'

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: After Jesus said these things, He went on ahead, going up toward Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
verses.modern: When He drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples ahead.

verses.kjv: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.
verses.modern: He said, "Go into the village ahead of You. As You enter, You will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here."

verses.kjv: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.
verses.modern: "If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' say this: 'The Lord has need of it.'"

verses.kjv: And they that were sent went their way, and found even as he had said unto them.
verses.modern: Those who were sent went and found it just as He had told them.

verses.kjv: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?
verses.modern: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are You untying the colt?"

verses.kjv: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.
verses.modern: They said, "The Lord has need of it."

verses.kjv: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus thereon.
verses.modern: They brought it to Jesus, threw their garments on the colt, and set Jesus on it.

verses.kjv: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
verses.modern: As He rode along, people spread their clothes on the road.

verses.kjv: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;
verses.modern: When He came near the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen.

verses.kjv: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
verses.modern: They said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"

verses.kjv: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.
verses.modern: Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, "Master, rebuke Your disciples."

verses.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.
verses.modern: He answered, "I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out."

verses.kjv: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
verses.modern: When He drew near and saw the city, He wept over it.

verses.kjv: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
verses.modern: He said, "If only you had known, even you, on this day, the things that make for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes."

verses.kjv: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
verses.modern: The days will come upon you when your enemies will build a wall around you and surround you from every side.

verses.kjv: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
verses.modern: They will level you to the ground — you and your children within you — and they will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.

verses.kjv: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;
verses.modern: He went into the temple and began to drive out those who were selling there.

verses.kjv: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.
verses.modern: He said to them, "It is written, 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of thieves."

verses.kjv: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,
verses.modern: He was teaching daily in the temple. The chief priests, the scribes, and the leading men of the people were seeking to destroy him.

verses.kjv: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.
verses.modern: But they could not find a way to do it, because all the people hung on every word he spoke.

chapters.summary: Zacchaeus the tax collector climbs a sycamore tree to see Jesus, and Jesus declares salvation has come to his house. Jesus tells the parable of the ten pounds and enters Jerusalem riding on a colt as the crowds praise God. He weeps over the city and drives the merchants out of the temple.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,
verses.modern: One day as He was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came up to Him with the elders.

verses.kjv: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?
verses.modern: They said to Him, "Tell us, by what authority are You doing these things? Who gave You this authority?"

verses.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:
verses.modern: He answered them, "I also will ask You a question. Tell me:"

verses.kjv: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?
verses.modern: "Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men?"

verses.kjv: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?
verses.modern: They discussed it among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why did You not believe Him?'"

verses.kjv: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.
verses.modern: "But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John was a prophet."

verses.kjv: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.
verses.modern: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.

verses.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
verses.modern: Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell You by what authority I do these things."

verses.kjv: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
verses.modern: Then He began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to farmers, and went away to a distant country for a long time."

verses.kjv: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
verses.modern: At harvest time He sent a servant to the farmers to collect some of the fruit. But the farmers beat Him and sent Him away empty-handed.

verses.kjv: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
verses.modern: He sent another servant, but they beat that one too, treated Him shamefully, and sent Him away empty-handed.

verses.kjv: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.
verses.modern: He sent a third, and they wounded Him too and threw Him out.

verses.kjv: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.
verses.modern: Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect Him when they see Him.'

verses.kjv: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
verses.modern: But when the farmers saw Him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, 'This is the heir. Let us kill Him so that the inheritance will be ours.'

verses.kjv: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?
verses.modern: So they threw Him out of the vineyard and killed Him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

verses.kjv: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.
verses.modern: He will come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others. When they heard this, they said, "May that never happen!"

verses.kjv: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?
verses.modern: He looked at them and said, "What then is this that is written: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone'?"

verses.kjv: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
verses.modern: "Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces. And when it falls on anyone, it will crush him."

verses.kjv: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.
verses.modern: The chief priests and the scribes wanted to arrest Him that very hour, but they feared the people. They knew he had spoken this parable against them.

verses.kjv: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.
verses.modern: They watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They hoped to catch Him in something He said, so they could hand Him over to the authority of the governor.

verses.kjv: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any, but teachest the way of God truly:
verses.modern: They asked Him, "Master, we know that You speak and teach correctly, and that You show no partiality. You teach the way of God truthfully."

verses.kjv: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?
verses.modern: "Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"

verses.kjv: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?
verses.modern: He saw through their trickery and said to them, "Why do You tempt Me?"

verses.kjv: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Caesar's.
verses.modern: "Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" They answered, "Caesar's."

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's.
verses.modern: He said to them, "Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God."

verses.kjv: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.
verses.modern: They could not trap Him in His words before the people. They marveled at his answer and were silent.

verses.kjv: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there is any resurrection; and they asked him,
verses.modern: Some of the Sadducees — who deny that there is a resurrection — came to Him and asked,

verses.kjv: Saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man's brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
verses.modern: "Master, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies, leaving a wife but no children, the man must marry the widow and raise up children for his brother."

verses.kjv: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
verses.modern: Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died without children.

verses.kjv: And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.
verses.modern: The second took her as wife, and he also died childless.

verses.kjv: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: and they left no children, and died.
verses.modern: The third took her, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.

verses.kjv: Last of all the woman died also.
verses.modern: Finally, the woman also died.

verses.kjv: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.
verses.modern: "In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife."

verses.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
verses.modern: Jesus said to them, "The people of this age marry and are given in marriage."

verses.kjv: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:
verses.modern: "But those who are considered worthy to reach that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage."

verses.kjv: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
verses.modern: "They can no longer die, for they are like the angels. They are children of God, being children of the resurrection."

verses.kjv: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
verses.modern: "That the dead are raised — even Moses showed this at the burning bush, when he called the Lord 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'"

verses.kjv: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.
verses.modern: "He is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all are alive to Him."

verses.kjv: Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.
verses.modern: Some of the scribes answered, "Master, you have spoken well."

verses.kjv: And after that they durst not ask him any question at all.
verses.modern: After that they did not dare to ask Him anything else.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David's son?
verses.modern: He said to them, "How can they say that the Christ is David's son?"

verses.kjv: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
verses.modern: "David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand,"'"

verses.kjv: Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.
verses.modern: "'until I make Your enemies Your footstool.'"

verses.kjv: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?
verses.modern: "David therefore calls him Lord. How then is he his son?"

verses.kjv: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,
verses.modern: While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,

verses.kjv: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;
verses.modern: "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at feasts."

verses.kjv: Which devour widows' houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.
verses.modern: "They devour widows' houses and for a show make long prayers. These will receive greater damnation."

chapters.summary: The chief priests and scribes challenge Jesus's authority, and He answers with the parable of the wicked husbandmen. They try to trap Him with questions about paying tribute to Caesar and the resurrection of the dead, but He silences them each time.

verses.kjv: And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.
verses.modern: He looked up and saw the wealthy putting their gifts into the offering box.

verses.kjv: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
verses.modern: He also saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.

verses.kjv: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
